subject: Kickoff: LAMP as an interpretable sequential-recs baseline
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off the LAMP evaluation track. Context: platform customers keep asking why their sequential recommendations do what they do, and our neural stack can't answer cheaply. Linear Additive Markov Processes are the counter-bet — a model that combines history states through an explicit linear mixture, so every prediction decomposes into readable per-step contributions. If LAMP holds up within a few points of the neural baseline, we ship it as the default interpretable tier.

Milestones (Feb 9 - May 25):
- Mar 13: reproduce the paper's experiments, starting with the Brightkite check-ins dataset per the released setup
- Apr 17: LAMP vs neural baseline on one internal sequential corpus, quality and cost side by side
- May 18: recommendation memo — adopt, adapt, or drop

Bao — staffing and any build-infra needs. It's a C++ codebase with gflags, so someone needs to own getting it into our bazel monorepo cleanly.

Dmitri
